source_text: Ergo Deum et iustum et pium credimus et veracem ac per hoc nihil impossibile mandasse legem eius tenemus, nihil falsum confirmare testimonia, nihil iniquum pronuntiare iudicia, sed ipsum esse hominum conditorem, quos nullo crimini obnoxios creat, verum plenos quidem innocentia naturali, voluntariarum autem virtutum capaces.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore we believe God both just and pious and truthful, and through this we hold that his law has commanded nothing impossible, that testimonies confirm nothing false, that judgments pronounce nothing unjust, but that he himself is the founder of humans, whom he creates liable to no crime, but full indeed of natural innocence, capable however of voluntary virtues.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: We therefore believe God to be just, good, and truthful. Consequently, we maintain that his law has commanded nothing impossible, his testimonies confirm nothing false, and his judgments pronounce nothing unjust. He himself is the creator of human beings, whom he creates liable to no crime, but full of natural innocence and capable of voluntary virtues.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
